question: What BLEU score does the Transformer achieve on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task?
in_doc: 28.4 BLEU (big model), over 2 BLEU above previous best including ensembles

question: How many layers are in the Transformer's encoder stack, and what sub-layers does each layer have?
in_doc: N = 6 identical layers; multi-head self-attention and a position-wise feed-forward network, each with a residual connection and layer normalization

question: What is the dimensionality d_model of the base Transformer model?
in_doc: d_model = 512

question: Why are the dot products scaled by 1/sqrt(d_k) in scaled dot-product attention?
in_doc: for large d_k the dot products grow large, pushing softmax into regions with extremely small gradients

question: How many attention heads does the base Transformer use, and what is the dimension of each head?
in_doc: h = 8 heads, d_k = d_v = d_model/h = 64

question: What kind of positional encoding does the Transformer use?
in_doc: sine and cosine functions of different frequencies; learned embeddings gave nearly identical results

question: Which optimizer and learning rate schedule were used to train the Transformer?
in_doc: Adam with beta1 0.9, beta2 0.98, epsilon 1e-9; learning rate increases linearly for warmup_steps = 4000 then decreases proportionally to the inverse square root of the step number

question: How long did it take to train the big Transformer model, and on what hardware?
in_doc: 300,000 steps, 3.5 days on 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs; base model 100,000 steps, 12 hours

question: What regularization techniques were used when training the Transformer?
in_doc: residual dropout (P_drop = 0.1 for base) and label smoothing (epsilon_ls = 0.1)

How does the computational complexity per layer of self-attention compare with recurrent layers?
in_doc: self-attention O(n^2 d), recurrent O(n d^2); self-attention faster when n < d; O(1) sequential operations vs O(n)

in_doc: 4-layer model on WSJ: 91.3 F1 WSJ-only, 92.7 F1 semi-supervised

Describe the three ways the Transformer uses multi-head attention.
in_doc: encoder-decoder attention (queries from decoder, keys/values from encoder output); encoder self-attention; masked decoder self-attention

question: How does the Transformer decoder prevent positions from attending to subsequent positions?
in_doc: masking: set illegal connections to -inf before the softmax; output embeddings offset by one position

question: What three desiderata do the authors consider when motivating the use of self-attention?
in_doc: total computational complexity per layer; amount of parallelizable computation (minimum sequential operations); path length between long-range dependencies

question: How did changing the number of attention heads affect translation quality in the model variation experiments?
in_doc: single-head attention is 0.9 BLEU worse than the best setting; quality also drops off with too many heads

question: What training data and batching were used for the English-German and English-French translation tasks?
in_doc: WMT 2014 EN-DE ~4.5M sentence pairs, BPE shared vocab ~37000 tokens; EN-FR 36M sentences, 32000 word-piece vocab; batches of ~25000 source and ~25000 target tokens

question: How does the Transformer handle embeddings and the softmax at its input and output?
in_doc: learned embeddings to d_model; shared weight matrix between the two embedding layers and the pre-softmax linear transformation; embedding weights multiplied by sqrt(d_model)

question: What beam search settings were used during inference for translation?
in_doc: beam size 4, length penalty alpha 0.6, maximum output length input length + 50, terminate early when possible

question: Why did the authors choose sinusoidal positional encodings instead of learned positional embeddings?
in_doc: nearly identical results; sinusoidal may let the model extrapolate to sequence lengths longer than seen in training; relative positions as linear functions

question: How does the maximum path length between positions in self-attention compare with recurrent and convolutional layers?
in_doc: self-attention O(1), recurrent O(n), convolutional O(n/k) contiguous or O(log_k(n)) dilated

question: How was the Transformer configured and trained for the English constituency parsing experiments?
in_doc: 4-layer transformer, d_model 1024, WSJ ~40K training sentences; semi-supervised with ~17M sentences; vocab 16K WSJ-only, 32K semi-supervised

question: How long did each training step take for the base models, and how long was the base model trained?
in_doc: about 0.4 seconds per step on 8 P100 GPUs; 100,000 steps or 12 hours

question: What is multi-head attention and why is it beneficial compared with a single attention function?
in_doc: h linear projections of queries/keys/values attended in parallel then concatenated and projected; lets the model jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions; averaging inhibits this with a single head

What is the purpose of the ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting?
in_doc: rules accompanying the ICD-10-CM conventions, approved by the Cooperating Parties, to assist provider and coder in identifying diagnoses to report; adherence required under HIPAA

question: Should signs and symptoms be coded when a definitive diagnosis has been established?
in_doc: signs and symptoms routinely associated with a disease process are not assigned as additional codes unless the classification instructs otherwise

question: What do the abbreviations NEC and NOS mean in ICD-10-CM?
in_doc: NEC = Not elsewhere classifiable; NOS = Not otherwise specified (unspecified)

question: What does an Excludes1 note indicate?
in_doc: a pure excludes note: the code excluded should never be used at the same time as the code above the note

question: How should a confirmed diagnosis of COVID-19 be coded?
in_doc: U07.1 COVID-19; confirmation by provider documentation, no test result required

question: When is the placeholder character X used in ICD-10-CM codes?
in_doc: as a placeholder for certain codes to allow future expansion, and where a 7th character is required but the code is not 6 characters long

question: How is severe sepsis coded?
in_doc: code the underlying systemic infection first, then R65.2- severe sepsis, plus codes for associated organ dysfunction

question: How is the principal diagnosis defined for inpatient admissions?
in_doc: the condition established after study to be chiefly responsible for occasioning the admission of the patient to the hospital for care (UHDDS)

question: How should uncertain diagnoses documented as probable or suspected be coded in the outpatient setting?
in_doc: do not code them as if established; code the condition to the highest degree of certainty, such as symptoms, signs or abnormal test results

question: How should hypertension with heart disease be coded?
in_doc: a causal relationship is presumed; assign a code from category I11 with an additional code for heart failure if present

question: What is the 7th character A used for in injury codes?
in_doc: initial encounter, used while the patient is receiving active treatment for the condition

question: How should diabetes mellitus be coded when the type is not documented?
in_doc: default to E11.- type 2 diabetes mellitus

How do the 'code first' and 'use additional code' notes work for conditions with an etiology and a manifestation?
in_doc: underlying etiology sequenced first, followed by the manifestation; 'use additional code' at the etiology, 'code first' at the manifestation; manifestation codes titled 'in diseases classified elsewhere' are never principal

question: What is the difference between an Excludes1 note and an Excludes2 note?
in_doc: Excludes1: never used together, conditions cannot occur together; Excludes2: not included here, patient may have both, both codes can be used together

question: How should a condition described as both acute and chronic be coded?
in_doc: if separate subentries exist at the same indentation level, code both and sequence the acute (subacute) code first

question: How are sequelae (late effects) coded?
in_doc: code the nature of the sequela (residual) first, then the sequela code; no time limit

question: How are pressure ulcer stages coded?
in_doc: combination codes in L89 identify site, stage and laterality; unstageable and unspecified stage codes; healing ulcers coded at their documented stage

question: How are the 7th characters D and S used in injury coding?
in_doc: D subsequent encounter after active treatment, receiving routine care during healing or recovery; S sequela, complications or conditions that arise as a direct result of an injury

question: How should hypertension with chronic kidney disease be coded?
in_doc: category I12 when both present, causal relationship presumed; additional code from N18 to identify the CKD stage

question: When should external cause codes be reported?
in_doc: no national requirement for mandatory reporting; encouraged; used for the length of treatment; may be used with any code in A00.0-T88.9, Z00-Z99 that represents a health condition due to an external cause

question: How is the principal diagnosis selected when two or more diagnoses equally meet the definition?
in_doc: any one may be sequenced first unless the circumstances of admission, therapy or the Alphabetic Index/Tabular List indicate otherwise

question: What are Z codes used for in ICD-10-CM?
in_doc: Factors influencing health status and contact with health services: reasons for encounters, circumstances other than a disease or injury, may be principal/first-listed or secondary

question: How should a patient admitted with an HIV-related condition be coded?
in_doc: principal diagnosis B20 HIV disease followed by additional codes for all reported HIV-related conditions

question: How should an encounter solely for chemotherapy for a malignancy be coded?
in_doc: Z51.11 encounter for antineoplastic chemotherapy as first-listed/principal, followed by the malignancy code
